messages:
Marta: Heads-up — I'm putting together the webinar landing + a lightweight battlecard focused on 'benchmarks -> buyer path -> routing'. Goal is to give field a 60s pitch vs CloudX/LLMAPI and a routing matrix for incoming leads. Doc: https://tinyurl.com/rwdb-webinar-draft
Devon: Love it. We need a 30s rebut when buyers say 'we already use managed endpoints' — short, tangible. Can we get 2 variations: SMB and Enterprise?
Ken: Suggest we lead with two measurable differentiators: predictable cost (committed/dedicated yields lower sustained unit cost) and routing/fallback that preserves uptime. Example phrasing: "Same API surface, predictable unit economics for steady workloads". Need final % numbers from infra bench.
Aisha: For the landing CTA, propose two flows: 1) "Request benchmark" -> routes to Bench SDR queue, 2) "Book demo" -> AE queue. Also add a microform field: "use case (chat/generation/embeddings)" to help route.
Riley: Battlecard snippets (for DMs/SDRs):
- Buyer: "We use CloudX managed endpoints"
  SDR: "Totally — many customers start there. Redwood keeps the dev DX but gives teams predictable capacity and fallbacks when CloudX throttles. We can run a quick cost/latency compare for your baseline."
- Buyer: "We can't manage infra"
  SDR: "You don't have to. Redwood Hosted + Dedicated options let you start with us and move to reserved capacity as you scale. We'll map the migration path."
Devon: Quick email nudge for post-webinar leads: 
``` 
Subject: Redwood bench offer — we'll run a 1hr comparison
Hi {{name}},
Thanks for joining. Want us to run a short bench against your sample workload? We'll return latency + unit-cost delta and a routing recommendation.
Schedule: [link]
```
Keep it under 2 sentences in body for quicker opens.
Marta: For the benchmark narrative — don't call out raw model names. Framing: "real app workloads, 2–3 sequence profiles, we optimize batching + cache to show unit cost impact." Ken: confirm we can share 'typical' percent ranges (e.g., 30–60% lower unit cost vs unmanaged endpoints for steady workloads) — if legal ok.
Ken: I'm clearing the numbers with infra, but we should phrase them as ranges and include a short note: "results vary by model, prompt length, and workload shape".
Aisha: Routing matrix idea: tag leads by CTA + keyword. If CTA=benchmark or message contains "latency"/"benchmark" -> BenchOps SDR, priority high. If CTA=demo or contains "SLA"/"enterprise" -> AE. If region=EMEA/APAC -> local rep first. I'll map HubSpot workflows and share IDs.
Riley: Add two-line play scripts to the battlecard: 1) Rebut + metric 2) CTA (bench/demo). Keep each under 140 chars for copy/paste.
Devon: Social copy (thread-sized): "Struggling with unpredictable inference bills? See how predictable capacity and smart routing keep apps online and costs down — join our benchmark webinar."
Marta: Awesome. Action items: Ken -> final percent ranges + short legal-safe blurb (EOD). Aisha -> HubSpot routing map + workflow IDs (tomorrow AM). Devon/Riley -> 6x two-line play scripts (SDR + AE) by EOD. I'll fold into the landing + battlecard and circulate.
ops-bot: created routing-draft #482 and assigned to Aisha (workflow: bench-sdr-route).
Devon: :thumbsup:
Marta: Thanks — will ping again after I merge the copy into the doc.
